claim: Paris Musée de la Magie sits in a 16th-century vaulted cellar, bundles 100+ animated automata, optical illusions and a short live magic show, and opens Wed/Sat/Sun 2-7pm (daily during zone C school holidays).
quote: mercredi, samedi, dimanche ... 14h-19h ... automates animés ... 100+ ... insolite

claim: Paris Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature is housed in a Marais mansion full of high-quality taxidermy including a standing polar bear, cheetahs, tiger and baby elephant, making it a surreal hunting-and-nature detour.
quote: sumptuously decorated rooms ... taxidermy specimens ... standing polar bear, cheetahs, a tiger, a baby elephant, wolves

claim: The Musée des Égouts de Paris takes visitors underground into ~500m of the operational sewer network; reopened after a major overhaul, it runs Tue-Sun 10am-5pm (last entry 4pm), closed 1 May, 25 Dec and the first half of January, €9 full / €7 reduced, free under-26 EU.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 5pm (last admission 4pm) ... €9 full price, €7 concessions ... free for minors and under-26s

claim: Amsterdam's Micropia (inside Artis) is the only museum in the world devoted entirely to microbes, with interactive exhibits that scan you to estimate the microbes living on your body.
quote: only museum in the world dedicated to microbes ... scan yourself to get a more or less correct estimate of the actual number

claim: Amsterdam's KattenKabinet (Cat Cabinet) is a 17th-century Herengracht canal house devoted to cats in art with works by Rembrandt, Picasso and Steinlen; a ~30-45 min visit, open Tue-Sun 12-5pm, €12.50 adults / €7.50 students / free under 12.
quote: Rembrandt, Picasso and Théophile Steinlen ... about 30-45 minutes ... open Tuesday-Sunday from 12pm-5pm ... 12.50 EUR for adults, 7.50 EUR for students

claim: Brussels' Sewer Museum (Musée des Égouts) walks visitors through a stretch of the real sewage network with an audio guide narrated by two sewer workers; open by appointment Wed-Sat 10am-5pm, from €10, free the first Sunday of each month.
quote: actual sewage network of Brussels ... audio guide narrated by two sewage workers ... on appointment Wed-Sat 10am-5pm, with prices starting at €10 ... free on the first Sunday of every month

claim: Brussels' Clockarium is a museum filled entirely with Art Deco ceramic mantel clocks, and the Brussels Comics Figurines Museum dedicates whole rooms to Smurfs, Tintin, Spirou plus manga and Marvel figurines.
quote: The Clockarium is a museum filled with Art Deco ceramic clocks ... Belgian comic book figurines like the Smurfs, Tintin and Spirou but also international figurines like Spiderman and Batman

claim: Bruges' Lumina Domestica (Lamp Museum) holds 6,000+ antique lamps tracing 400,000 years of indoor lighting from torches to LEDs, including a section on bioluminescent animals and plants.
quote: More than 6,000 antiques tell the complete story of interior lighting, from the torch and paraffin lamp to the light bulb and LED ... glow-worm, the lantern fish

claim: Bruges' Frietmuseum is the world's first and only museum dedicated to Belgian fries, set in the medieval Saaihalle with a cellar café; admission €12 adults / €10 seniors-students / €7 children 3-11, with a €0.50 fries discount.
quote: Adults pay €12.00, seniors (65+) and students €10.00, children (3-11) €7.00 ... a € 0.50 discount on a portion of fries (in the basement)

claim: Antwerp's Museum Plantin-Moretus, a UNESCO site, is the preserved 16th-century home-and-workshop of the Plantin-Moretus printing dynasty, holding the two oldest printing presses in the world and the only surviving original Garamond letter dies; it closes for renovation 3 Aug-4 Dec 2026.
quote: two oldest printing presses in the world ... world's only copy of the original Garamond letter dies ... closed for renovation work from 3 August to 4 December

claim: Antwerp's Snijders & Rockox House merges two adjacent 17th-century patrician homes of painter Frans Snijders and collector-mayor Nicolaas Rockox, presented as a lived-in house with an iPad guide rather than a conventional gallery.
quote: combines the former residences of painter Frans Snijders and Nicolaas Rockox ... feels more like a former home than a traditional gallery ... iPad that is given to visitors

claim: Antwerp's Red Star Line Museum, set in the line's authentic former dockside buildings, tells the story of the millions of European emigrants who sailed from Antwerp to North America in the early 20th century.
quote: story of Europeans who travelled to Antwerp to take Red Star Line ships to emigrate to North America ... housed in the authentic buildings
